clue.text: No entrance to shelter in leafy glade

indicators.note: no entrance means the word for shelter loses its opening letter

parts.note: a harbour is a shelter, especially for ships

explanation.surface: A clearing among trees offers shelter but has no way in.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady bower formed by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Silly response missing one of the points in note

indicators.note: missing means the response word goes without one letter

parts.note: an answer is a response
W is west, one of the compass points
taken as written
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A foolish reply lacks something written in a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: ANSWER loses W, the compass point, to give ANSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anserine means goose-like, hence foolish or stupid.

clue.text: One who dips into fuel tanker without right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tanker word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a bowser is a British tanker for fuel or water

explanation.surface: Someone siphoning from a tanker without any right to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser reads casually, sampling here and there.

clue.text: Use big letters for a drug container

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a case is a container

explanation.surface: Shout in capitals about a pill box.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters were kept in the upper case of a printer's type.

clue.text: Though not a scholar, Pitt the Elder was a great one

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and some other universities a student without a scholarship is so called

definitions.text: Pitt the Elder was a great one
definitions.meaning: William Pitt the Elder, an 18th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: Pitt the Elder may not have been a scholar, but he was great at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a student paying full fees and a person without a title, as Pitt famously long remained.

clue.text: Horse in the main chase may be one of the Queens

parts.note: the main is the open sea
a grey is a horse of that colour
to hound is to chase

explanation.surface: A horse in a chase at sea might be royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queens are the Cunard liners Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast passenger liner was called by that name, as those Cunard ships were.

clue.text: State to run internal railway

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: internal puts the run letter inside the word to

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The government runs a railway at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground or city railway system.

clue.text: Tin mounting the Spanish and French use for engine casing

indicators.note: mounting means going up, so in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can
el is Spanish for the
le is the definite article the French use

explanation.surface: Fixing a tin with Spanish and French parts for an engine cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing for an aircraft engine.

clue.text: Smack with gusto

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a tasty flavour and keen enjoyment.

clue.text: A letter head for libertarianism

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per day
a missive is a letter
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A head writes a note in favour of freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerance of freedom of behaviour, close to libertarian views.

clue.text: Splendid example of a bit of theatre

indicators.note: a bit of theatre places the bit after the theatre word

parts.note: a show is a theatrical production
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A fine sample taken from a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding item displayed as a model of its kind.

clue.text: 22 had a pound coin once

parts.note: the answer to 22 down is bursts of activity, and a tic is a nervous spasm
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Spasms came with an old pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' sends you to 22 down: one such spasm is a TIC. 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tical was a former silver coin and unit of currency of Siam (Thailand).

clue.text: Funny sort with a peculiar snout

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of sort are rearranged

parts.note: rum is old British slang for strange or peculiar

explanation.surface: An odd character with a strange nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like it describes the sort of person, but it is the anagram signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostrum is the zoological term for a beak or snout-like projection.

clue.text: Food one sold minced

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so the letters are cut and remixed

explanation.surface: Someone sold food that had been minced.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta dough, a staple food.

clue.text: The woman takes last name from the man

indicators.note: taking the last N (name) from the man's name removes that letter at the end

parts.note: Norman is a man's name

explanation.surface: A wife adopts her husband's surname.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; it is taken from the end of NORMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a girl's name, so it can stand for a particular woman.

clue.text: One who could hold his audience spell-bound

definitions.text: One who could hold his audience spell-bound

parts.words: One who could hold his audience spell-bound
parts.note: spell-bound read literally: a magician who binds people with actual spells rather than captivating them

explanation.surface: A gripping performer keeps the crowd entranced.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard casts spells, so his listeners are literally bound by magic.

clue.text: It enables one to draw a gun

definitions.meaning: a goal that levels the score lets a team draw
slang for a pistol, which levels odds

explanation.definitionFit: A levelling goal brings a draw, and old gangster slang uses the same word for a revolver.

clue.text: Colleague given new medical speciality becomes a rival

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or mate
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A coworker retrains in medicine and turns competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is an adversary or competitor.

clue.text: It's a condition hard to endure, according to one heartless Tory

parts.note: as per means according to
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative without compassion says life is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes OR from the middle of TORY, leaving TY. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity means harshness or severity, as of a climate or circumstance.

clue.text: Detailed proposal for development in Japan

indicators.note: development means the remaining letters are worked into a new form
de-tailed means the word proposal loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A thorough scheme for growth in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' cuts L from PROPOSAL; 'development' rearranges PROPOSA. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapporo is the largest city on Hokkaido, a place in Japan.

clue.text: Take the lid off a French international

parts.note: un is the French for a
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for a national team, so an international

explanation.surface: Open a bottle with a French national player.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player selected for their country is said to win a CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncap is to remove a cap, a lid or cover.

clue.text: Prime Minister recording in advance

definitions.meaning: George ... was British prime minister in 1827
putting on film or tape beforehand, as material is said to be in the can

explanation.definitionFit: The statesman's surname matches preserving a recording, from the film jargon of having it in the can.

clue.text: Many sulphur 'springs start bursts of activity

indicators.note: start means the springs word comes first

parts.note: spas are mineral springs
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphurous hot springs begin to erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden brief bursts of effort or activity.

clue.text: A little Indian puzzle about a river

indicators.note: about means the puzzle word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to pose is to puzzle
the Po is the river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A small Native American child is set a riddle near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little Indian' reflects dated usage; the word comes from Narragansett, a Native American language.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American baby or young child, in dated usage.

clue.text: "Beware of false prophets" — only some refuse

indicators.note: only some of the words means just part of their letters run together

explanation.surface: A biblical warning that only a little of what you're given is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal can mean refuse or waste matter, as well as animal entrails.

clue.text: Novel title in gold letters

annotationWithheld.why: Novel title in gold letters (7): ORLANDO is the Woolf novel, OR gold, but no sound parse found for the rest ('title' as LAND inside ORO? 'letters' as L and O?)

clue.text: Food that is mouldy

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
food gone off is mouldy

explanation.surface: Some food has gone mouldy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is British slang for food, from the verb to eat greedily.

clue.text: Girl queen could be in teens

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A girl might become queen while still a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' is the whole definition: the answer is a given name, not a description of a teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a female given name.

clue.text: Virgin with a clear complexion

explanation.surface: An innocent with flawless skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmarked is pure, and a face without blemishes is unmarked too.

clue.text: One who makes women virtuous

parts.note: right means morally good, upright

explanation.surface: A craftsman makes women upright.
explanation.walkthrough: A wright is a maker, as in playwright or shipwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Wright is an old word for a craftsman or builder.
